# Research pack: Northwind Regional Health ERP pursuit (synthetic, M1 demo)

## Buyer strategic context

source: https://example.org/synthetic/demo-strategy-brief
Northwind Regional Health is consolidating back-office platforms after a
multi-year clinical systems program, and its board has funded a single
ERP implementation workstream covering finance, supply chain, and human
capital management. Public statements stress go-live reliability over
speed, and the program office has been directed to hold vendors to
rehearsed cutover plans with explicit fallback criteria.

## Vendor landscape and incumbent signals

source: https://example.org/synthetic/demo-vendor-landscape
No implementation incumbent holds the account; a national advisory firm
completed the platform selection and is barred from delivery under the
buyer's conflict rules. Two integrators active in the regional market have
publicized health-system ERP go-lives in the past year, one of which was
publicly criticized for a payroll disruption during cutover weekend.

## Procurement and financial signals

source: https://example.org/synthetic/demo-financial-signals
The capital plan reserves funding for a phased implementation with
milestone-based payments and formal gate reviews between phases. Recent
procurement notices show the buyer favors fixed-fee phases, requires
named-key-personnel commitments, and scores transition risk and local
support presence heavily in its published evaluation criteria.
